identity.name: Vạn Xuân (Early Lý dynasty)
alt_names: Nam Việt (the Lý Nam Đế page's name for the state)

land.text: Jiaozhou (Giao Châu): the Red River delta with Thanh Hóa and Nghệ An, the Liang province Lý Bí's rising took in 541–543

predecessors.note: The infobox names the 'Second Era of Northern Domination' as predecessor; the Liang were the power Lý Bí revolted against.

land.text: Jiaozhou, surrendered by Lý Phật Tử to Liu Fang's army in 602

capitals.name: Long Biên
capitals.note: Infobox: Long Biên, in modern Hanoi; 'in the winter of 545, Chen surprised the capital' (Lý Nam Đế page) and the court fought on from Gia Ninh (fell 546) and the hills. Coordinates are the researcher's (Bắc Ninh side of the delta).

capitals.name: Dạ Trạch (Khoái Châu swamp)
capitals.note: Triệu Quang Phục 'based his forces in a swamp' in the Red River Delta; 'Dạ Trạch' is his title in the page's citation 8. Coordinates are the researcher's (Khoái Châu, Hưng Yên).

capitals.name: Phong Châu (Việt Trì)
capitals.note: 'Phong Châu' is cited as Lý Phật Tử's capital (citation 8) without a year; placed from his victory of 571. Coordinates are the researcher's.

keyframe_review.note: Years only: from February 544, when 'Lý Bí was declared emperor of Nam Việt', not 546 (the year Gia Ninh fell). 92,427 km2 is Jiaozhou: the Red River delta with Thanh Hóa and Nghệ An to the Lâm Ấp frontier; no infobox area to compare. The Liang reoccupation of the delta 545–550 is hatched, not a border change.

90,334 km2; the trim of the northern edge (23.30 to 23.04 N) coincides with Cliopatria's Chen dynasty row (561); no page explains it and the two courts of 557–571 (Triệu in the delta, Lý Phật Tử in the west) are not drawn as a split. Within precision.
Years only: to 602, when 'Lý Phật Tử surrendered' to Liu Fang; Cliopatria ends the row in 601.

region.text: Jiaozhou (Giao Châu): the Red River delta with Thanh Hóa and Nghệ An

ledger.note: 544: Lý Bí proclaims himself emperor of Vạn Xuân. 'Lý Bí resigned his post and revolted in 541 against the Liang dynasty', 'won a decisive battle in Hepu in summer 543, expelling the Liang from Northern Vietnam region', and 'in February 544, Lý Bí was declared emperor of Nam Việt'; the Early Lý page: 'In 544, Lý Bí defeated the Liang, proclaimed himself emperor, named the state Vạn Xuân'. The Early Lý infobox dates the revolt 541, its body 543. The boundary is Cliopatria's Jiaozhou.

region.text: the Red River delta, Jiaozhou's core, with the capital Long Biên

ledger.note: 544: the Liang send an army to retake Jiaozhou. 'In October of 544 the Liang dynasty sent an army to reoccupy Jiaozhou'; 'By spring of 545, Chen had ravaged much of Jiaozhou'. Blend (rule 6) over the delta until 550.

region.text: the Red River delta, Jiaozhou's core, with the capital Long Biên

ledger.note: 545: Chen Baxian takes the capital. 'in the winter of 545, Chen surprised the capital during the monsoon season'; 'In 546, Gia Ninh fortress fell, and Lý Bí's army fled into guerrilla warfare' (Early Lý page); 'In 547, Lý Nam Đế was assassinated' (Early Lý page) against 'By April 548 ... Lý Nam Đế died somewhere in Northwest Vietnam' (Lý Nam Đế page). Hatched: the Liang hold the delta while the Lý fight from the hills and swamps; the extent held is the researcher's reading.

548: Lý Bí hands power to his brother Lý Thiên Bảo; Triệu Quang Phục takes the throne in the delta. 'In February 548, he relinquished imperial authority and transferred his power to his older brother'; 'On April 13, 548, Triệu Quang Phục ascended the throne as Triệu Việt Vương' (Early Lý page, citation 8). Same state, same colour (rule 2); the two courts (Triệu in the delta, Lý Thiên Bảo then Lý Phật Tử in the west) are a split the pages do not map.

region.text: the Red River delta, Jiaozhou's core, with the capital Long Biên

ledger.note: 550: the Liang driven out. 'The new king continued the resistance and eventually drove the Chinese out from Vạn Xuân in 550'; the Early Lý page: 'The indecisive period ended in 557, when the Liang were distracted by the Hou Jing rebellion'.

region.text: the Red River delta, Jiaozhou's core, with the capital Long Biên

ledger.note: 550: the war with the Liang ends in Vạn Xuân's favour. 'drove the Chinese out from Vạn Xuân in 550'.

571: Lý Phật Tử defeats Triệu Việt Vương and reunites the state. 'In 571, Lý Phật Tử broke the truce and attacked Triệu Quang Phục's domain. Triệu Quang Phục died by suicide during the retreat'; infobox: Lý Phật Tử 'regained the throne in 571'. Same state, same colour.
571: the court at Phong Châu. 'Phong Châu' is cited as Lý Phật Tử's capital without a year; placed at his victory of 571.

602: Lý Phật Tử surrenders to the Sui. 'In 602, Lý Phật Tử bribed the governor Lệnh Hồ Hy, and Emperor Wen of Sui ordered Liu Fang to invade with 100,000 troops. Lý Phật Tử surrendered'; infobox: surrender of Hậu Lý Nam Đế 602. Cliopatria ends the row in 601; the reign list adds Lý Sư Lợi (603).

wars.name: Liang–Vạn Xuân war (544–550)

zones.text: the Red River delta, Jiaozhou's core, with the capital Long Biên

wars.outcome: The Liang army sent in October 544 took the capital in the winter of 545 and Gia Ninh in 546; Lý Bí died in 548; Triệu Quang Phục 'drove the Chinese out from Vạn Xuân in 550'.
wars.note: Chen (Chen Baxian, the later founder of the Chen dynasty) led the Liang army.

wars.name: Sui conquest of Vạn Xuân (602)
wars.outcome: 'Emperor Wen of Sui ordered Liu Fang to invade with 100,000 troops. Lý Phật Tử surrendered.'

certainty.note: The state is the Liang province of Jiaozhou; its northern limit follows the provincial frontier Cliopatria draws, its southern limit toward Lâm Ấp (Đức Châu, Hà Tĩnh) is approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Early Lý Dynasty' 546–601 (3 shapes) kept as one dossier, dated 544–602 from the pages (Cliopatria's 546 is the year Gia Ninh fell). The 561 trim of the northern edge is unexplained by any page. The Liang reoccupation 545–550 is an occupation (hatched), the 544–550 war a contest over the delta.

Not on the pages opened (traditional accounts a gap-filler could verify from 'Phạm Tu' or 'Triệu Việt Vương'): the 543 Lâm Ấp invasion of Đức Châu (Hà Tĩnh) defeated by Phạm Tu; the Battle of Điển Triệt lake (546); Lý Thiên Bảo's and Lý Phật Tử's western court at Dã Năng (555–571), which with Triệu Việt Vương's delta court would be a split the map could draw if a page gave its extent; Lý Sư Lợi's 603 remnant. Disagreements: Lý Bí's death 547 (Early Lý page) or April 548 (Lý Nam Đế page); the revolt 541 (infobox) or 543 (body); the end of the Liang presence 550 (Lý Nam Đế page) or 557 (Early Lý page).

Requests to other dossiers: liang-dynasty (ea-03) should carry the loss of Jiaozhou in 544 and the occupation 545–550; sui-dynasty (ea-03) the gain in 602; champa's 543 war is not recorded here because no page opened gives it. Gazetteer: 'Red River Delta' resolves.
